fase-1: Create a production-ready transparent PNG pixel-art sprite animation sheet for a classic Ben 10 beat-em-up. The attached three-figure reference is the exact character design. Match it closely: Forever King adult human face visible under wide swept black HORNED helmet, black royal cape crimson lining, red gold-edged tabard, mint diamond Excalibur sword. Do NOT use a soldier T-visor or invent a different face. Use the existing game sprite style of the reference: strong dark outlines, deliberately clustered pixel shading, arcade three-quarter side view FACING RIGHT. Only TWO arms and TWO legs. All poses are separately DRAWN anatomically coherent full-body keyframes, no duplicate stills or tiny translations of the same image. Every pose's entire silhouette, sword tip, horns, cape and crystal fragments must fit well inside its cell. Very generous empty separation. NO grid lines, NO labels, NO text, NO ground or shadows or background. EXACTLY SIX COLUMNS, evenly spaced fixed cell centers; each ROW is ONE action with SIX successive chronological frames LEFT TO RIGHT. Within a row fixed character scale and consistent baseline, no fake camera zoom. Keep sword reach within the cell, leave generous right margin. A polished coherent animation sheet, not a mood board. SQUARE SHEET, exactly SIX ROWS by SIX COLUMNS = 36 complete full-body poses, every cell occupied. Use ONLY LEFT reference phase 1 design: INTACT substantial mint diamond plates on chest, shoulders, forearms, shins, shining long straight crystalline Excalibur sword with golden crossguard. Character is proud and measured, not clumsy. ROW1 idle loop: steady guarded breathing, cape hem shifts, hand tightens on hilt, shoulders subtly rise and settle through six distinct poses. ROW2 slow heavy WALK: six true alternating footfall poses, hips, knees and cape move, sword carried diagonally ahead, planted feet not sliding. ROW3 heavy sword slash: clear anticipation sword back, winds up, blade travels downward across front, full extension contact, follow-through, returns to guard. ROW4 defense block: raises Excalibur across chest, braces behind crystal pauldron, takes a blow, recoils half-step, re-centers guard, lowers sword slightly; no magic sphere covering the body. ROW5 EXPOSED STAGGER loop: sword hangs low, shoulders heave, wide exhausted stance, exposed hand on cracked chest, clearly vulnerable through six different weight shifts, armor stays largely intact. ROW6 DEFENSE BREAK transition: braced guard, a few cracks flash across mint breastplate, sword arm knocked aside, head recoils, drops onto ONE knee with sword tip planted to right, last pose vulnerable crouch. Armor still on, not fully shattered! Crystal pieces sparse and within cell. Every row's body is exactly the same scale, no frame cut off.
